问题:
Hello.
I purchased your product https://www.amazon.es/dp/B07RY6HTF5?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1

To replace the receiver on my ceiling fan https://faro.es/es/coleccion/easy-ventilador-de-techo-gris/

Everything seems fine except for one thing. The speeds are too fast. How can I reduce the speed of each of the three fan speeds?

Thank you
答案:
Hello, the fan speed is higher than expected due to a compatibility issue between the fan motor and the running capacitor; this is not a fault with the controller. This product comes standard with a 2.5 μF start capacitor and a 3 μF running capacitor;
Here are 3 suggestions:
Option A: Replace your fan’s original ‘start capacitor’ with a model of slightly lower capacity (for example, replace the 2.5 μF capacitor with a 1.5 μF capacitor).
Option B: Alternatively, you could remove the fan’s capacitor first, connect the QIACHIP controller, and check whether the fan speed adjusts.
Option C: You can connect a capacitor in parallel at the QIACHIP controller’s input port; this will act as a current limiter, causing the fan’s overall speed to gradually decrease.
Please use electricity safely, and ensure that all attempts are carried out with the assistance of a professional.
We hope this helps resolve your issue. Thank you.

问题:
The unit has been working fine for the last couple of weeks, but today the fan does not work on the 'low' setting. Med and Hi are fine.
1. Switch the power on at the wall
2. Press the low setting on the remote (the fan spins at high speed for a few seconds, then slows down to a stop)
Thanks
答案:
Here’s what’s happening in simple terms: when you press low, the fan first spins fast for a few seconds — this is the controller giving it a quick boost to get started, then it drops down to low speed. The fact that this boost works, and medium/high speeds run perfectly, means the remote and controller are working fully as they should.
Low speed runs on lower power, so it has very little extra strength to keep spinning. When a fan gets older, or builds up extra resistance from dust or worn internal parts, low speed is always the first one to struggle and stop, while higher speeds still work fine.
Please try these 3 simple checks:
1. Turn the wall switch off for 60 seconds, then turn it back on and test low speed again to rule out a temporary glitch.
2. With the power off, spin the fan blades by hand. If they feel stiff or don’t spin freely, the fan motor has built up resistance over time — this is very common on older fans.
3. Double-check that all wire connections inside the fan canopy are tight. Loose wires cause a small power drop that only affects the low speed setting.    他再次回复：Thank you for your email and the troubleshooting advice. 
I tried your tips, but the problem persisted, in fact I noticed that both med and hi buttons now make the fan go in high-speed mode only.
When I installed the remote a few weeks ago it worked perfectly,  we were very happy.

问题: So this product works great. Easy to install and instructions to disable beep are clear. 问题:
Hi,
I msg to say that the 'low' setting on our fan controller had stopped working. Well, now both Med and Hi are running at the same speed. This was working brilliantly for a couple of weeks, clearly something has failed.
Kins regards
答案:
Thanks for the detailed description, and we’re sorry for the trouble with the low speed setting.
Here’s what’s happening in simple terms: when you press low, the fan first spins fast for a few seconds — this is the controller giving it a quick boost to get started, then it drops down to low speed. The fact that this boost works, and medium/high speeds run perfectly, means the remote and controller are working fully as they should.
Low speed runs on lower power, so it has very little extra strength to keep spinning. When a fan gets older, or builds up extra resistance from dust or worn internal parts, low speed is always the first one to struggle and stop, while higher speeds still work fine.
Please try these 3 simple checks:
1. Turn the wall switch off for 60 seconds, then turn it back on and test low speed again to rule out a temporary glitch.
2. With the power off, spin the fan blades by hand. If they feel stiff or don’t spin freely, the fan motor has built up resistance over time — this is very common on older fans.
3. Double-check that all wire connections inside the fan canopy are tight. Loose wires cause a small power drop that only affects the low speed setting.
问题的英文翻译: Hello. I previously reported that LOW on our fan controller had stopped working. Now MED and HI also run at the same speed. It worked very well for a couple of weeks, but something has clearly failed. Kind regards.

问题: Hi, I installed the QIACHIP ceiling fan remote control (featuring 3 speeds, light control, and 4 timer settings for 220V/230V ceiling fan lamps), but there is hardly any difference between the LOW and HIGH fan speeds. Curiously, the highest speed occurs at the MID setting. Can you help us with this issue? The previous controller provided a higher fan speed. Thanks.
答案:
Hi,
Before installing the controller, please switch off the power at the mains for safety.
If your ceiling fan has an original speed control, please make sure it is set to the highest speed (High) before connecting our receiver.
Depending on your fan model:
• Pull chain: Pull the chain until the fan is running at the highest speed (usually High is the fastest setting).
• Wall switch or wall speed controller: Move the speed switch or slider to the highest (High) position.
• Rotary speed knob: Turn the knob fully to the maximum speed.
If your fan has only an ON/OFF wall switch and no built-in speed selector, no adjustment is required.
Also, please leave the original light switch ON before using our remote control.
